A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same corpus-reformulation study, renamed from MAGA to MGA. Their text, tables, figures, equations and appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original corpus-quality evaluations, pretraining and scaling experiments, prompt ablations and token-loss analyses in Sections 4–5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original training and analysis results and adds experiments comparing models trained on MGA, Cosmopedia and Nemotron-CC corpora in Table 4.

M1.justification: The two-stage generation process, five genre-audience pairs per document, 3.3B MoE tool models, Limited Consistency criterion and heuristic cleaning remain unchanged. Section 3.3 reorganizes existing prompt variants; Appendix E retains their substantive instructions.

E1.justification: Table 4 extends training-source coverage to Nemotron-CC reformulations, including wiki-style transformations of lower-quality web text and knowledge/QA transformations of high-quality web text. Cosmopedia was already used in v1 mixtures. Downstream tasks and language coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 adds a dedicated comparison against Cosmopedia and six Nemotron-CC configurations in Table 4, substantially expanding direct evaluation against alternative synthetic-data approaches. These were not dedicated comparators in v1. The small-LM comparator set in Table 3 is retained.

E3.justification: Table 4 introduces a 377M-model, 300B-token comparison protocol, matching MGA and Cosmopedia at 28B unique tokens repeated 10.7 times. Appendix C also changes the stated MMLU setting from 0-shot to 5-shot, although Table 3 scores remain unchanged and rerunning is not established. Existing main training budgets and mixing weights are retained.

E4.justification: The multi-dataset validation-loss analysis drops the MGA-Only trajectories: v1 Figure 6 includes three training recipes, whereas v2 Figure 5 includes only Baseline and MGA-Expansion. Prompt ablations, t-SNE analysis, synthetic-only benchmark comparisons, anomaly analysis and English/Chinese case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The token-loss standard deviation used in Appendix D.3's anomaly definition is unchanged.

E6.justification: New Table 4 substantially expands comparative results: reported averages are 37.28 for MGA versus 35.57 for Cosmopedia, and 37.34 for MGA versus 40.72 for Nemotron's diverse QA pairs; MGA exceeds the other five Nemotron configurations. Table 3 values remain unchanged. v2 also fills three previously blank quality-rate entries and removes MGA-Only validation-loss trajectories.

T1.justification: Appendix D.3 retains the token-loss difference, absolute windowed anomaly threshold and normalized-position definitions. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced; the expanded scaling discussion is conceptual.

C1.justification: v2 adds an introductory contribution claim about improvements over training on other synthetic datasets and emphasizes mitigation of data repetition. The central claims about the 770B-token corpus, benefits over repetition/upsampling and limitations of validation loss remain.

C2.justification: v2 attributes Nemotron QA's advantage to alignment with predominantly 0-shot evaluation, without directly testing that explanation. It removes v1 Section 5.2.3's specific hypothesis about human editing and competition between reasoning and memory, while retaining the broader generalization-versus-memorization interpretation. Appendix A adds a qualification about hallucinated errors and biases surviving filtering.

D1.justification: v2 newly tabulates per-source unique-token counts and repetition epochs for existing recipes, names LM-Harness and updates the dataset access address. It reduces the FineWeb preprocessing description from global min-hash deduplication to generic deduplication. Tool-training details, model hyperparameters and hardware-cost estimates are largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Gao et al.'s evaluation framework and the SmolLM article while retaining the main related-work coverage. The introduction newly distinguishes augmentation from large-model distillation, and Section 4.3.1 develops direct positioning against Cosmopedia and Nemotron synthesis strategies.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten around repetition and augmentation. MAGA/MAGA-Mix become MGA/MGA-Expansion, research questions are reorganized, and former ablation/discussion material is distributed across Sections 3.3 and 4.3. Training recipes and appendix analyses are extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 adopts colored headings, a boxed abstract and extensively reformatted tables and captions. It adds Table 4, expands recipe tables, relocates the implementation diagram and scaling panels, enlarges retained displays, revises Figure 3's legends and adds a zoomed inset to Figure 4. These constitute a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Table 4 addresses part of v1's lack of direct comparisons with alternative synthetic corpora, including a matched-token Cosmopedia comparison and evidence that Nemotron QA performs better. Clearer organization and explicit recipe accounting also improve assessability. The gain is limited by the new comparisons' single model size, the untested QA-format explanation and the removal of MGA-Only validation trajectories.
